hints.title: Single Deletion Branching State Choice
hints.text: You can optionally remove at most one element from the subarray. What state distinction captures whether a deletion has already occurred?

hints.title: Zero Versus One Deletion Invariant
hints.text: Maintaining two running totals: one where no elements were deleted, and one where exactly one element was skipped, enables single-pass optimal transitions.

hints.title: Dual State Transition Procedure
hints.text: For each element, transition the one-deletion state as the maximum of skipping the current element (previous zero-deletion total) or extending a previous deletion. Transition the zero-deletion state as standard restart or extension. Track global maximum across both states.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maximumSum(self, arr: List[int]) -> int:
        no_del = arr[0]
        one_del = 0
        ans = arr[0]
        for i in range(1, len(arr)):
            x = arr[i]
            one_del = max(no_del, one_del + x)
            no_del = max(x, no_del + x)
            ans = max(ans, no_del, one_del)
        return ans
```

variables: N: input element count or target integer bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Trying all O(N) possible deletions and running Kadane each time takes O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual-state tracking calculates the optimal solution in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should correctly handle non-empty subarrays and track zero-deletion vs one-deletion transitions.
